title: Artemis II Crewed Lunar Flyby — 13-Phase Free-Return Simulation
architectureStatus: Complete 13-phase crewed lunar flyby and figure-eight free-return trajectory simulation inspired by NASA's Artemis II mission. Orion flies around the Moon without landing.
publishedFacts: Artemis II is NASA's first crewed flight of the Space Launch System (SLS Block 1) and Orion spacecraft, carrying four astronauts: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.

SLS Block 1 launches from Launch Complex 39B with 8.8 million pounds of liftoff thrust, separating twin Solid Rocket Boosters at ~2 minutes, Service Module fairings and the Launch Abort System shortly after ~3 minutes, and the Core Stage at ~8 minutes.
After an initial ~90-minute Earth orbit and solar array deployment, the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) raises Orion into a High Earth Orbit (~24-hour period) for systems checkout.
Orion separates from the ICPS and performs an interactive Proximity Operations demonstration using the spent ICPS and adapter as a handling target.

Orion's European Service Module performs the Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI) burn, sending the crew on a ~4-day outbound transfer and a figure-eight free-return trajectory passing ~4,600 miles (~7,400 km) beyond the lunar far side (>240,000 miles from Earth).

While behind the Moon, Orion experiences an expected geometric radio blackout (~43 minutes) before emerging with restored Deep Space Network communications and returning to Earth on a gravity-driven ~4-day return arc.

Prior to Earth Entry Interface (~75.7 miles / 121.9 km altitude at ~25,000 mph), the Crew Module separates from the Service Module, experiences ~4G peak deceleration and ~5,000°F peak Avcoat heat-shield temperature, deploys an 11-parachute sequence (3 FBC, 2 drogues, 3 pilots, 3 mains), and splashes down below 20 mph in the Pacific Ocean (~50 NM off California) for U.S. Navy recovery.
trainingAssumptions: The trajectory uses a deterministic 3-segment patched-conic figure-eight free-return model (outbound Kepler transfer -> Moon-centred retrograde hyperbolic flyby at 7,400 km perilune -> return Kepler transfer to 121.92 km Earth Entry Interface).
The Moon follows a 384,400 km orbit inclined 5.145 degrees to the equator with nodal alignment for the translunar transfer window.
SLS launch uses a continuous guided ascent profile (T-15s to T+510s) with ROFI, RS-25, SRB, fairing, LAS, and Core Stage staging events.
Atmospheric entry integrates point-mass skip-entry aerodynamics with lift-modulated deceleration capped near ~4.0G and heat-shield temperature peaking near ~5,000°F.
Time acceleration advances the underlying physical simulation state continuously without skipping phase guards or checks.
epoch: Simulation epoch T-15s at terminal countdown; T+0s at SLS liftoff.
units: SI internally (m, s, kg, N, rad); HUD displays both metric (km, m/s, kg) and imperial reference units (miles, ft, mph, °F, M lbs).

frames.ECI: Earth-centred inertial, equatorial XY, Z north
frames.MCI: Moon-centred inertial, axes parallel to ECI
